record.what_it_does: Work management platform for boards, items, and workflows across teams.
record.auth_notes: Personal V2 API token goes in the Authorization header. OAuth app tokens are scoped, don't expire in the legacy flow, and have no refresh tokens. A newer OAuth 2.1 flow adds refresh tokens. A multi-user toolkit would use OAuth.
record.access_notes: The auth page says a free developer account gives a token for testing. I did not confirm whether public distribution of an OAuth app needs marketplace review. The OAuth docs list "Submit your app to the marketplace" and "App review checklist" pages, which I did not open. Plan requirements for API use are not stated on the pages I read.
record.api_breadth_notes: Single GraphQL endpoint at api.monday.com/v2 with a public schema. It covers boards, items, columns, groups, updates, webhooks, users, workspaces, docs and more. I did not count operations.
record.mcp_notes: npm package @mondaydotcomorg/monday-api-mcp, run with npx and authenticated with an API token. The page I read marks it beta and lists no hosted URL. A vendor-hosted remote MCP (mcp.monday.com) may also exist. I could not confirm it from the docs I fetched.
record.blocker_notes: There is a public GraphQL API, free developer account tokens and OAuth. The only open question is whether public distribution of an OAuth app needs marketplace review. I did not confirm this.

evidence.quote: Personal V2 API token ... App tokens have a defined set of permission scopes; free developer account to get a token and start testing.
Tokens do not expire and are valid until the user uninstalls your app.
The monday.com API uses GraphQL and exposes a single endpoint, https://api.monday.com/v2
Requests sent through our webhook integration will retry once a minute for 30 minutes.

record.needs_human: Three things to check: (1) whether public OAuth apps need marketplace review before other accounts can install them; (2) whether a hosted remote MCP (mcp.monday.com) exists; (3) whether API access is restricted by plan or rate limits. The sandbox "yes" is a judgment call: the auth page says a free developer account is available for testing, but I did not open a page that describes sandbox accounts.
